descriptionChirho: Adjective meaning free, liberated, or released from bondage/obligation, used of manumitted slaves (Exod 21:2, 5, 26, 27; Deut 15:12, 13, 18; Jer 34:9–16), freed prisoners (Isa 58:6), and the dead who are 'free' from earthly concerns (Job 3:19; Ps 88:6). The second cluster (S98533, 3 occurrences) uses the prepositional phrase לַחָפְשִׁי 'to the free [state]' meaning 'to freedom/liberty,' but the lexeme itself retains its adjectival sense of 'free.' Multilingual evidence confirms a single meaning: eng 'free/freedom', spa 'libre/libertad', hin स्वतंत्र/स्वतन्त्रता, arb حُرّ, kor 자유로운, swa 'huru/uhuru.'
